identification: Passage parallel to Cherubino da Spoleto, Sermones quadragesimales; compiling text and attribution unresolved
note: Selected manuscript line ends agree with a Google Books snippet labelled PA346 for the 1502 edition. Full printed page unavailable; shared source and catalogue dating unresolved.

catalogue_title: Unidentified commentary on the Book of Genesis

identification: Johannes Balbus, Catholicon, letter C
note: Catapuera, Catapulta and Cataracta definitions and sequence compared with edition n211; additional Catalecticus group inspected. Full range and leaf order unchecked.

identification: Nicholas of Lyra, Postilla litteralis super Epistolam ad Hebraeos, chapter 5
note: Pontifical-office explanation and office-seeking warning match the 1603 print, cols.841–842, with local wording differences. Complete endpoints remain unverified.

identification: Richard of Middleton, Quaestio disputata de gradu formarum; leprous-parent and asses arguments
note: Leprous-parent and asses arguments match the published excerpts in Hocedez, with manuscript/print differences and an uncertain cancellation. Full collation and witness novelty remain unresolved.

institution: Leuven, Archief van de Abdij van Park
catalogue_title: Gloss on unidentified canon law text
identification: Guido de Baysio, Rosarium super Decreto, C.10 q.1 c.13
note: Connected manuscript passage matches the 1481 print, image 0415 (206a). Faded material leaves the broader c.14/q.2 span unverified.

catalogue_title: Commentarium super IV librum Sententiarum (unidentified), dd. 15
identification: Anonymous Sentences IV epitome combining mnemonic verse and prose summaries
note: Verse block matches pseudo-Bonaventure, Peltier VI p.655; punishment list parallels Hus edition p.593. Edition OCR used; compiler and direction of borrowing unresolved.

catalogue_title: Unidentified theological treatise, containing a fragment of Summa Theologiae
identification: Anonymous compilation adapting Aquinas, Summa theologiae IIa-IIae q.10 a.12 and q.11 a.1
note: Natural-justice and heresy passages parallel Aquinas, with condensation and added legal references. The catalogue’s q.10 a.11 locus is outside the checked sample.

identification: Alphabetical compilation of moral authorities, with Moralium dogma philosophorum and patristic source parallels
note: Connected Modestia passage and patristic quotations support source connections. Shared quotations, including one in the Manipulus florum, do not identify the compiler.

identification: Anonymous scholastic questions probably relating to Sentences I; author and exact locus unresolved
note: Innascibilitas and generation arguments checked against related Richard of Middleton and Thomas of Strasbourg discussions. Topic shared across authors; exclusive school attribution unsupported.

identification: Unidentified Latin didactic poem on sacramental themes, with an apparent dieta transition
note: Selected sacramental and dieta passages are readable, but no sustained source match is established. Adam of Aldersbach’s Summula remains an untested candidate.

identification: Hippocrates, De regimine acutorum, with Galen commentary in the Latin Articella tradition
note: Lemma and sustained commentary checked against 1491 Articella n181, with additional passages and a clause transposition. Translator, book numbering and full endpoints unresolved.

identification: Bernardus Compostellanus iunior, Lectura in primum librum Decretalium, De electione
note: De novo and Querelam/Removeri passages checked against actual 1516 print images n125–127, fols.55v–56v. Local abbreviation and lemma uncertainties remain.

identification: Robert Holcot, Super Sapientiam Salomonis, end of lectio II and part of lectio III
note: Three connected commentary passages compared with actual 1494 print images n40–41. Wording variants retained; unread binding areas and complete endpoints unchecked.

identification: Anonymous procedural text with a close Durantis, Speculum iudiciale II.3, De appellationibus parallel
note: Durantis II.3 n.14 shares a case with different wording; the n.15 continuation differs. Exact work and recension remain unresolved.

identification: Medical compilation on sleep, with Hippocratic and other source layers; compiler unidentified
note: Albert the Great’s sleep narrative and Hippocratic aphorisms supply parallels, with different Latin wording. The proposed Arnoldus Saxo witness remains uncollated.

institution: Leuven, KU Leuven Bibliotheken Bijzondere Collecties
identification: Commentary around Hippocrates, Aphorisms VII.54–59, plus a medical chapter table; compiling work unresolved
note: Selected aphorisms agree with Articella OCR. The surrounding commentary, exact chapter-table text and translator remain unresolved; Galen is not excluded.

identification: Anonymous Metaphysics questions with sustained Aquinas, Sententia libri Metaphysicae VII lect.4 nn.3–4 parallels
note: Man/whiteness and proportional-participation passages parallel Aquinas’s digital Latin text; the question apparatus is distinct. A digitized Versor witness remains uncollated.

identification: Anonymous questions on longevity, natural heat and moisture in the Parva naturalia tradition
note: Questions concern natural heat, moisture and longevity. Related Buridan passages differ; exact base text and author remain unresolved.

institution: Leuven, Archief van de Abdij van Park
catalogue_title: Legendary: unidentified life of St Gregory the Illuminator, ch. 3-7
identification: Latin life of Gregory the Illuminator in the Agathangelos tradition; exact Latin recension unresolved
note: Mule/altar and baptism sequences compared with the longer Acta Sanctorum life; Latin wording differs. Anonymous BHL3664 checked and differently abbreviated, not an exact match.

institution: Leuven, Archief van de Abdij van Park
catalogue_title: Legendary: unidentified legend on St Gregory the Illuminator, ch. 1-5
identification: Ending of a Latin life of Gregory the Illuminator; exact Latin recension unresolved
note: Princely retinue, Rome and Nicaea narrative compared with longer Acta Sanctorum life; source-family connection supported but wording differs. BHL3664 ending also checked.

catalogue_title: Unidentified commentary on a religious text
identification: Unidentified, heavily worn text; a scholastic lemma-and-exposition commentary is plausible
note: Abrasion leaves the image readings uncertain; no continuous passage is secure enough to establish a source match.

dimensions: 292 mm x 210 mm, 292 mm x 68 mm
institution: Scherpenheuvel-Zichem, Abdij der Norbertijnen van Averbode, Archief
identification: Sermon for the seventh Sunday after Trinity (Mark 8, feeding of the four thousand); collection unidentified
note: A numbered literal exposition of the gospel (points six to twelve survive) followed by a distinction on mercy to three kinds of people, borrowing Compendium theologicae veritatis I.34. Thesaurus novus de tempore has the same scheme in other words and was seen in snippets only; Herolt differs. Right-column passage read by the coordinator, the rest by a second reader.

identification: Pharetra doctorum et philosophorum, section De amore inimicorum
note: Entries of the clearer face, with source labels, the cross-reference quere supra de amore proximi and the Decretum note, agree with the Mentelin print (not after 1472), Munich copy fols. 39v–40v, page images directly compared. Author groups stand in a different order on the leaf. Not the pseudo-Bonaventure Pharetra; Manipulus florum excluded. Faded face read by a second model only.

institution: Leuven, KU Leuven Bibliotheken Bijzondere Collecties
identification: Peter of Spain, Tractatus XI De restrictionibus, or a commentary following it closely: sophism Omne animal fuit in archa Noe
note: Recto has the past-tense restriction rule and the opening of the sophism; verso its solution with pro singulis generum / pro generibus singulorum, same phrases in the same order as the Tractatus. Leaf torn to half-lines and compared with edition snippets only; a commentary or variant version is not excluded. Reader report from the 11 October recheck; not rechecked by the coordinator.

identification: Scholastic text on the four causes; unidentified
note: Not law. Recurrent causa efficiens, formalis, materialis, finalis, materia et forma, Notandum est quod, Quantum ad secundum across four canvases; no three consecutive secure lines, so no source search was possible. Reader report from the 11 October recheck; not rechecked by the coordinator.

shelfmark: Archief Schepenbank Mechelen aan de Maas, nr. 2
identification: Johannes Serapion the Elder, Breviarium medicinae, tract VII, chapter XX; upper-cover leaf
note: Upper-cover faces match the recipe sequence and distinctive cumin/pepper commentary in Serapion, Venice 1497, fols. 71v–72r. Avicenna shares the cumin prose but not the surrounding sequence. Manuscript and edition images directly checked; lower-cover leaf remains unchecked. Separate assisted reading preserved.

institution: Leuven, Archief van de Abdij van Park
identification: Petrus Hispanus (non-papa), Summa "Absoluta cuiuslibet" (grammar): on devocatio and on ille as demonstrative or relative
note: Lower recto and whole verso of one leaf follow Kneepkens's 1987 edition pp. 8-10 in order at seven points (devocatio defined; ille qui scripsit Georgica scripsit Eneida; semini tuo qui est Christus; tu es ille Eneas quem genuit Venus), with small variants of wording. Compared with Google Books search-inside snippets, saved in audits; edition pages not seen; other leaf too faded. Grammar, not logic as catalogued. Assisted readings preserved.

identification: Lectura on Codex 7.53, De executione rei iudicatae, ll. 4–9; author unidentified
note: Runs through l. Stipendia, l. Etiam nomen, l. Executorem and l. 9; cites Jacobus de Ravanis and Raphael Fulgosius, so after about 1420. Printed Paulus de Castro has the same doctrine in different wording; Fulgosius, Salicetus and Baldus on the title not checked. Not ff. de rei vindicatione. Reader report from the 11 October recheck; not rechecked by the coordinator.

identification: Not identified
note: Both faces and upper native-to-supplied-image crops inspected. Severe abrasion and staining permit only uncertain fragments. Catalogue links HS.2583/074, /078 and /084 as possible same-manuscript fragments; those companions remain unchecked. A rain/grace analogy in Caesarius, Dialogus miraculorum II.1, surfaced during other research, but a source-assisted recheck did not establish a continuous match. Stop: no diagnostic reading; different-light images or specialist reading required. Recheck, 11 October: only a bracketed list of lines beginning fluvium was legible; still no diagnostic reading.

identification: Scholastic question on consequentiae; unidentified
note: Numbered conclusiones on formal consequence, the conditional si homo est chimera est, and a reference to the materia insolubilium; not matter and form. Legible only in patches; no five connected lines and no search match. Reader report from the 11 October recheck; not rechecked by the coordinator.

institution: Scherpenheuvel-Zichem, Abdij der Norbertijnen van Averbode, Archief
identification: Question-commentary on Peter of Spain, Tractatus; commentary unidentified
note: Lemma Individuum est quod de uno solo predicatur is Peter of Spain tract II, not Porphyry; another leaf argues on contradiction, conversion and supposition. Cologne and Paris printed commentaries neither confirmed nor excluded. Pieces may derive from more than one manuscript. Reader report from the 11 October recheck; not rechecked by the coordinator.

identification: Possibly a sermon or postil on John 20:19–21; unidentified
note: One column reads pax vobis ... sicut misit me pater et ego mitto vos ... misit me ad passionem; readings are tentative and the rest gave isolated words. No source found. Reader report from the 11 October recheck; not rechecked by the coordinator.

identification: Probably Godfrey of Fontaines, Quodlibet V q. 12, or an abridgement of it
note: Three places on the recto follow the argument of Quodl. V q. 12 (De Wulf–Hoffmans 1914, pp. 52–54) in order, without verbatim agreement; one of the three (iuvenes liberales ... non obediunt verecundie) is Godfrey borrowing Aquinas on Ethics X and does not distinguish them. One passage spot-checked by the coordinator. Verso unread.

identification: Bifolium of sermons de tempore: Advent sermon on Matthew 11 and Christmas Vigil sermon on Cras faciet Dominus; collection unidentified
note: The Exultet line is a quotation in the Vigil sermon. The Advent sermon moralises John's two messengers as contrition and confession, with the exemplum of a woman weeping before an altar seen by a demoniac. No printed collection matched; Caesarius is not the containing work. Reader report from the 11 October recheck; not rechecked by the coordinator.

identification: Lemmatised commentary on Priscian, Institutiones XVII 42–45; commentary unidentified
note: Not law. Lemmata Sic igitur adverbiorum, ut qualiter, ad generales et speciales, Est preterea notandum, ut quisquis follow Priscian XVII 42–45 (Keil III 133–135) in order; the earlier lombar reading is teutonicus, lombardus, examples of gentile adjectives. No printed commentary matched. Catalogued host text is not the wrapper's text. Reader report from the 11 October recheck; not rechecked by the coordinator.

identification: Question-commentary on angels (Utrum angelus sit in loco; species universaliores); work unidentified
note: Fol. [4]r reports the view that angels are in place per operationem as what aliqui say and seems to argue against it; fol. [1]r has Angeli superiores habent species universaliores quam inferiores. Wording matches no searched text; Aquinas is a doctrinal parallel only. Three canvases dark, two not zoomed. Reader report from the 11 October recheck; not rechecked by the coordinator.

catalogue_title: Unidentified gloss, possibly on a grammatical treatise
identification: Commentary on Alexander de Villa Dei, Doctrinale, chapter 8, vv. c. 1262–1279; commentary unidentified
note: Red-marked lemmata on one face follow the Doctrinale in order (Quae sine persona, Postulo posco, Hiis obliviscor, Hiis iungas, Adde per et; Reichling pp. 82–83), with glosses on verbs taking two accusatives. Grammatical, as catalogued; not a Psalm gloss. The commentary's prose was not read well enough to search. Reader report from the 11 October recheck; not rechecked by the coordinator.

catalogue_title: Unidentified commentary on the Psalms (?) / Credo
identification: Upper musical text contains the Creed; lower text is a lemmatic commentary on Psalm 50:7–16, unidentified
note: Lower text comments Ecce enim, Asperges me, Auditui meo, Cor mundum, Docebo iniquos, Libera me de sanguinibus in order, so Psalm 50 and not Psalm 118, against which the first pass compared it. Distinctive wording (valet hic locus contra Arrianos; spiritum principalem ... ultimo loco posuit) found in no searched corpus; Bruno the Carthusian and Remigius differ on Docebo iniquos. Reader report from the 11 October recheck; not rechecked by the coordinator.

identification: Sermon or tract on shame in confession with two exempla; work unidentified
note: One face carries an ordeal exemplum (a wife carries hot iron unharmed after confessing, relapses, and is burned by the same iron cold) and a Vitae patrum exemplum of a youth who tells his mother he will save his soul; the earlier reading monachus dicebat anime sue was wrong. No matching text found; other face too abraded. Reader report from the 11 October recheck; not rechecked by the coordinator.

identification: Bernard of Parma, Casus longi super Decretales, book III: casus on X 3.4.11–12 and X 3.5.5–6
note: Consecutive casus on both faces agree in wording and sequence with the casus printed beside X 3.4.11–12 and X 3.5.5–6 in the Turin 1588 glossed Decretals (OCR text compared; page images and a separate Casus longi edition not collated). Author by the standard ascription of those casus. Assisted reading preserved.

identification: Galen, De sanitate tuenda (medieval Latin De regimine sanitatis), book VI, translation attributed to Burgundio of Pisa.
note: Two continuous main-text passages on fol. [1]v match Pinzi 1490, vol. II, fols. 179v–180r, including connecting prose and symptom sequence. Both manuscript/edition image pairs checked by two Codex readers. Printed Galen/Rufus caveat and scholarly translation attribution recorded separately. Marginal glosses unresolved; no human review.

identification: Canon-law commentary within the Decretals title De accusationibus (X 5.1), on inquisition; work not identified
note: Binding cover rubbed to a ghost. Only one area of the back cover gives words ("infamatus", "inquisitio", "ex officio", a citation of c. Qualiter et quando); no connected five-line stretch could be read and four phrase searches gave generic hits. Front cover unread. Model readers only.

institution: Scherpenheuvel-Zichem, Abdij der Norbertijnen van Averbode, Archief
identification: Notabilia on Gratian's Decretum, Causae 31-32; the collection is not identified
note: Entries are canon incipits followed by "Nota quod" or "argumentum quod", running C.31 q.1 to C.32 q.5 with red Causa numbers and marginal quaestio numbers. Two argumenta also stand in the Glossa ordinaria (1595 print, Google Books snippets) but most entries do not, so it is not the gloss. About ten distinctive phrases matched nothing in Google Books, archive.org or Corpus Corporum. Canon order placed from the lemmata, not checked against Friedberg.

identification: Tabula utriusque iuris attributed to Johannes de Erfordia, article Appellatio (on tacit renunciation of an appeal)
note: Three passages, two consecutive, agree with Bremen, SuUB, msa 0137, f. 27v (page images; coordinator compared about fourteen lines), and most of the recto was placed at f. 26r by the research reader. Not the same form of the text: the case is reworded (ad papam ... ad ordinarium), citations, sigla and order differ. A second witness, Bruges Grootseminarie 46/57 f. 31v, agrees with Bremen against the leaf and adds Sext citations; recension of the leaf not decided. Unprinted; attribution is the catalogues'. Kurtscheid 1914 not seen. Excluded on page images: Monaldus (Pal. lat. 695) and the short article of Pal. lat. 804.

identification: Twelfth-century treatise on consequences and hypothetical propositions with sophisms and their solutions; not identified
note: The author's own plan survives on fol. 2v ("Tocius ordinis expeditio ... Adiunximus vero oppositiones tam solubiles quam insolubiles ... Insolubilium autem solutiones nullas assignabimus"). About thirty phrases matched nothing in Google Books or archive.org, nor inside De Rijk, Logica Modernorum II.2 and three other volumes (snippets); individual sophisms recur in edited texts in other words. Probably unedited. Canvases after the first four were downloaded but not read.

identification: Bede, De temporum ratione, chapter 43 (fol. F)
note: Twenty-seven lines of fol. F recto follow Giles vol. 6 pp. 232-233 (OCR text) in order, and the first lines of the verso continue the chapter; coordinator checked lines 10-19 on the image. Variants include calculatorum and discernerent; not compared with Jones's edition. The first image-only reading used canvases that do not show fol. F. The sideways leaf in the same images (Priscian, Institutiones XIV) belongs to record F-fwl6. Stub before fol. D unread.

dimensions: Front Pastedown: 145 x 205 mm; Back Pastedown: 166 x 120 mm;
identification: Prose tract on construction and regimen (double accusatives, De regiminibus, gerunds and supines, impersonal verbs); not identified
note: A magister weighs opinions in the first person ("quibus consentimus"); the last chapter opens "Ultimo videamus de constructione inpersonalium" with three etymologies of impersonalia. Closest printed parallel is Gutolf of Heiligenkreuz's Summa grammatica as excerpted by Schönbach (1904, OCR): one shared sentence, but a different chapter order, mnemonic verses and examples. No match in Bursill-Hall's Census (snippets), Thurot (OCR), Google Books or archive.org. Untested for want of text: Dybin's Regimina and other unedited regimen tracts.

catalogue_title: Alexander of Hales, Summa Theologica; unidentified theological text
identification: Wrapper made from four manuscripts: Summa Halensis III (as catalogued), Juvencus with glosses, a Lenten gradual, and an unidentified text on giving out of pietas
note: Front strip: six consecutive lines match Summa Halensis III, exposition of the Nicene Creed, Quaracchi IV p. 1133 (snippets). Sideways sheets: Juvencus, Evangeliorum libri, Praefatio 4-10 and I 10-14, with glosses (Corpus Corporum; from the first reading, not re-read). Neumed pieces: gradual, Lent IV and Passion Sunday (from the first reading). Back strip unidentified: Valerius Maximus V.1.9 and V.1.8 as exempla, in wording close to Cessolis; John of Wales has the same pair in other words; Peraldus weakly negative; Vincent of Beauvais untested.

institution: Chicago, University of Chicago Hanna Holborn Gray Special Collections Research Center
identification: Short model sermons on the Sunday gospels after Pentecost (Lucan pericopes), not a commentary on Luke; collection not identified
note: Openings include "Duo homines ascenderunt in templum. Videamus quid templum, qui gradus templi et qui illi duo homines significent" (checked on the image) and "Videns Ihesus civitatem ... ter flevit". None is in the nine Schneyer volumes as searchable on archive.org, nor in Patrologia Latina by proximity search.

identification: Aldobrandinus de Toscanella, Scala fidei (sermons on the Apostles' Creed): Tertia die resurrexit and Sedet ad dexteram
note: Two passages, one on each leaf (about 13 and 20 lines), agree with Vatican, BAV, Pal. lat. 449, ff. 167ra and 172va, page images read by a research reader and compared by the coordinator; small variants. Work unprinted; Schneyer I nos. 350-380 (snippets), no. 364 incipit as on the fragment. Attribution after Schneyer and Kaeppeli 1938. Other columns not compared.

dimensions: VS + fliegendes Bl.: 108 × 160 mm; HS: 110 × 80 mm
identification: Sermon or distinction material ("Renovatur homo quot modis"; authorities on bearing burdensome people); not identified
note: The flyleaf passage on renewal (the stag that draws in the serpent and runs to the spring; the white garment at baptism) recurs reworded in the fifteenth-century Hungarian Sermones dominicales (ed. Szilády 1910, snippets), a later derivative or shared source. The pastedown's chain of authorities matched nothing. Not a biblical commentary.

identification: Scholastic question on the receptacles of souls (sinus Abrahae, limbus patrum and puerorum), about 1235-1260; not medical; not identified
note: Every line is cut. Ruled out by reading OCR: Albert, IV Sent. d.1 a.20 and d.44 a.45, and De resurrectione. Weak negatives on snippets: Alexander of Hales's Glossa IV, William of Auxerre, Thomas, Bonaventure, Peter of Tarentaise. A parallel unprinted "Questio de locis animarum exutarum" is excerpted in Scholastik 24 (1949) pp. 546-557, not seen in full.

identification: Abbreviated sermons (Ps 76:11 "Hec mutatio dextere excelsi"; a Good Friday sermon on six effects of Christ's blood); not identified
note: Only the bottom nine or ten lines of each column survive. No hits in Google Books, archive.org or Corpus Corporum; Schneyer I lists the Psalm theme three times, none with this development. A later cursive addition abridges the Legenda aurea on Mary Magdalene (recognised, not collated).

identification: Letter formulary (wife to absent husband and his reply with Ulysses and Penelope; kin and student letters); not identified
note: Too pale for five secure consecutive lines. Ruled out by OCR keyword search: Rockinger's Briefsteller und Formelbücher and Guido Faba's Dictamina and Epistole. Untested: Boncompagno, Bene, Laurentius of Aquileia, Thymo, Dybinus. A library stamp and shelfmark are visible in the images the first reader saw.

identification: Digest of John of Freiburg, Summa confessorum IV, rearranged under Decretal titles; the digest is not identified
note: Cases ending "hec Wil." follow Summa confessorum IV tit. 7 and tit. 21 q. 3 in shortened wording (1518 print, snippets). Display headings are Liber Extra IV titles and the cut list is Book III titles. Ruled out: Astesanus (snippets), Summa rudium (OCR). Small paper bifolium in a personal cursive; a private excerpt notebook is possible. No five consecutive lines read securely.

identification: Exposition of the Decalogue with exempla (heretics; feast-breaking); not identified
note: The three recto exempla (Theoderic's deacon, Olimpius in the bath, Gregory VI's doors) all stand in Martinus Polonus's Chronicon and are retold in the compiler's words. Weak negatives on incunable OCR: Nider, Herp, Alexander Carpentarius. Untested for want of searchable text: Henricus de Frimaria, Herolt, Dinkelsbühl, Ebendorfer.

institution: Chicago, University of Chicago Hanna Holborn Gray Special Collections Research Center
identification: Rhymed verse rendering, with rubrics and canon-law gloss, of Raymond of Penyafort, Summa de casibus I.1 De simonia; the versification is not identified
note: Six units on both sides follow Raymond's paragraphs VIII-X in order (Verona 1744 pp. 12-14, OCR), and the marginal gloss gives Raymond's allegations. Not Adam's Summula (three prints searched; BnF lat. 15162 f. 56r read on the page is Adam's). No verse found in Google Books, archive.org or Corpus Corporum. The Villers chronicle says Arnulf of Louvain versified the Summa and that work is reported unrecovered; nothing survives to compare, so this is not an attribution.

identification: John of Abbeville, sermons for saints' days: Sicut exaltavit Moyses serpentem and Ego quasi vitis (Nativity of the Virgin)
note: All four columns are one continuous passage agreeing with Charleville-Mézières BM 218, ff. 38r-40r (IRHT microfilm page images), about 120 lines in three stretches read by a research reader; the coordinator compared two places on the images. Schneyer 3 p. 529 nos. 271-272 (snippets). Work unprinted. The side labelled v precedes the side labelled r. A sermon collection, not a biblical commentary.

identification: Abbreviated scholastic notes, including the question whether the intellect can know truth without special divine illumination; not identified
note: Photographed upside down; the first reader gave only a layout survey and a second isolated reader read a rotated packet. One passage answers the question as Duns Scotus does (Ord. I d.3), so notes on I Sent. d.3 in a Scotist order are a lead. The other side is abraded. No verbatim match.

institution: Scherpenheuvel-Zichem, Abdij der Norbertijnen van Averbode, Archief
identification: Question-commentary on Peter of Spain, Tractatus V (De locis), close to the Cologne Copulata; the commentary is not identified
note: The "amator sapientie ... desiderator" argument and reply, and the "nullum animal currit" argument, run parallel in content and order to Lambertus de Monte's Copulata (Cologne 1487 and 1494, OCR) in other words; one argument on totum integrale is Versor's. No printed commentary matches verbatim for five lines: also tested Johannes de Magistris, Tartaret, Marsilius and an anonymous Scotist exposition (OCR); Bricot's OCR was too corrupt to test; Gerardus de Harderwijk and the Louvain commentaries were not found online. The subject of the first argument is read "rusticus" or "iustus"; the letters are ambiguous. Probably a student reportatio of Cologne Thomist teaching.

identification: Scholastic sermon on James 1:25 "non auditor obliviosus factus sed factor operis"; not identified
note: About half the surface is illegible at the available resolution. Readable members ("premium copiosum ... premium beatificum"; "quelibet res habet propriam operacionem") matched nothing in Google Books, archive.org or Corpus Corporum. Schneyer by theme not tested.
